packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 19 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of the work or author reached me before or during this reading. I did not search, consult editions, or open anything except PROMPT.md and the images.
- I did list the packet directory (ls) to get the image filenames. I opened nothing else in it except PROMPT.md and the images; I did not read packet.json.
- Provenance-type information I saw anyway: the working directory path contains "stams3". A modern pencil note in the gutter of both faces also reads roughly "Stams, STA, Frg. 131r" (image-009, face A) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 131v" (image-025, face B). These are archival/shelfmark notes, not identifications of the text. I did not use them.
- All 32 images loaded. Image-001 and image-017 are reduced overviews of the two faces (A and B). Images 002-016 are tiles of face A and 018-032 are tiles of face B, in three rows of five, overlapping their neighbours.
- Line numbers below are counted from the top of the overview (image-001 for face A, image-017 for face B), column by column. Each column has 30 lines. I checked every reading against the native tiles and name the confirming tiles for each column. Lines that repeat in overlapping tiles are one line, not extra text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- This is a bifolium photographed open on both sides: two pages per face, two columns per page, so four columns per face with about 30 ruled lines each. The centre fold has slits/sewing holes, and the inner margins are worn.
- There are no running titles in the visible upper margins. The top edge of face A's right-hand page is torn at the gutter.
- Two text sizes alternate. Larger blocks of prose are in a bold, compact late-Caroline/early-Gothic book hand. Smaller-script passages carry staffless neumes above the line (adiastematic/in campo). A small rubricated "a" or "R" (R/ and V/ signs) sometimes sits inside or beside an initial.
- There are red initials (two lines high, sometimes larger) and red rubrics and abbreviated cue words (for example "OR", "Ad uesp(eras) Cap(itulum)", "Inv.", "In mat(utinis) laud(ibus)", "f(eria) vi", "viii", "Ad copl."). Face B col. 4 has a large red O with a drawn face inside.
- A neumed section opens on face A col. 1 with a large red H containing R/.
- In the outer margins there are small pen sequences such as "11.SP.", "1·1·0", "11nas", "BS". They look like tone/differentia-type cues or later marks. I did not interpret them.
- Face A col. 1: "MARIE" is not on this face. Face B, left margin by col. 1 line 18: "MARIE" in small capitals with a small cross above it.
- Face B, in the intercolumn between cols. 3 and 4: a long vertical cursive annotation in a later hand, partly numerals ("154..", "R 4 R"?), mostly [illegible].
- Tentative interpretation: a liturgical office book (lessons, chapters, collects, neumed antiphons and responsories). I have deliberately not tried to name the work, the feasts or the date.

SELECTED AREAS
I read all eight columns, both faces, in full where the leaf allowed. What remains unread or uncertain:
- Face A col. 3: the inner (gutter) ends of most lines are abraded and stained, especially lines 1-5 and 14-30.
- Face B col. 2 line 1 and line 25: cramped and partly rubbed rubric and initial cues.
- The intercolumn annotation on face B.
Conventions: "(et)" is the tironian sign. Expansions are in parentheses. [red] marks rubricated items. "?" follows uncertain readings.

LIMITATIONS
- Face A col. 3 is the weakest witness: the first letters of most lines are abraded at the gutter, and lines 1-5 and 22-30 have real gaps. I did not fill those from sense.
- The top line of each column may follow lost text, because the leaf is trimmed at the top and no catchwords or running heads are visible. The bottom lines run on.
- I have not settled the column/page order across the bifolium (which page follows which). The order above is simply left to right as photographed.
- I recorded neumes only as present or absent; I did not transcribe them.
- Several rubric abbreviations ("f.", "eu", "cap." signs, red single letters) are read tentatively.
- Suggested follow-up: a raking-light or multispectral image of the gutter on face A (right page), and a closer crop of the face B intercolumn annotation and of face B col. 2 lines 1 and 25.
